title: EFTA, Vietnam wrap up comprehensive FTA negotiations
summary:
EFTA and Vietnam have concluded negotiations on a comprehensive Free Trade Agreement covering goods, services, investment, intellectual property, government procurement, rules of origin and sustainable development. 
The agreement aims to reduce trade barriers, improve market access and strengthen economic cooperation. 
Footwear and apparel remain among the EFTA's leading imports from Vietnam.

title: Eurostat reports steady euro area unemployment in May
summary:
Eurostat reported the euro area unemployment rate at 6.2 per cent in May 2026, unchanged from April and down from a year earlier. 
The EU rate held at 5.9 per cent, with 13.163 million people unemployed across the bloc.  
Youth unemployment edged up in the EU but held steady in the euro area, a labour signal for sourcing teams.

title: India’s home textile exports fall 20% as China holds 43% share
summary:
TexPro data show India’s home-textile recovery is lagging despite broader textile export resilience.
US imports fell 20 per cent YTD, while India’s bed linen, terry towels and blankets remain well below trend.
China continues to dominate key markets, indicating that trade deals and cotton-duty relief alone are unlikely to revive demand without stronger retail recovery.

title: Upland, Pima cotton export decline sharply: USDA
summary:
US cotton export sales weakened in the week ended June 25, with Upland bookings falling 42 per cent week on week and Pima sales dropping to a marketing-year low, USDA data showed.
Upland shipments also declined, while Pima exports climbed to a seasonal high. Vietnam, India and Pakistan remained the leading destinations for US cotton exports.

title: Drewry WCI further rises 8.7% on tight capacity, strong demand
summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index rose 8.73 per cent to $4,530 per FEU, driven by higher Transpacific and Asia-Europe freight rates amid strong demand and tight capacity.
Carriers continue to announce rate increases and surcharges, with Drewry expecting further gains.
Geopolitical risks in the Middle East continue to support elevated shipping costs.

title: Italy's Ferraro acquires Cibitex finishing unit
summary:
Ferraro has acquired Cibitex’s textile finishing business unit, strengthening its portfolio of finishing technologies and technical expertise.
The deal secures continuity for customers, partners and employees while expanding Ferraro’s international capabilities.
The transaction closed on July 2, 2026, supporting both companies’ long-term growth strategies.

title: ICE cotton ends lower on weak US export report
summary:
ICE cotton futures snapped a three-day rally, with the December 2026 contract settling 0.92 per cent lower at 77.12 cents/lb as weak US export sales outweighed support from a softer dollar.
Despite the fall, the contract gained 74 points for the week.
Analysts expect prices to remain range-bound between 75 and 80 cents amid sluggish demand and thin holiday trading.

title: Functional Fabric Fair to spotlight sustainable sourcing in NYC
summary:
Functional Fabric Fair Summer 2026 will bring together over 150 global suppliers, connecting sourcing teams with the latest performance and sustainable materials.
The event features a dedicated sustainability workshop, expert-led sessions, networking and innovations for the Summer 2027/2028 apparel seasons across activewear, outdoor, swim and lifestyle categories.

title: Bharat Tex 2026 to showcase India's textile strength globally
summary:
Bharat Tex 2026 will bring together over 7,000 buyers, 1.3 lakh trade visitors and 1,600 exhibitors, reinforcing India's position as a global textile sourcing and investment hub.
With 3,500 curated B2B meetings, 100-plus knowledge sessions, international delegations and strong state participation, the event is set to boost trade, sourcing, investment, innovation and global partnerships.

title: Bangladesh’s banking crisis: The $15.6bn supplier exposure map
summary:
TexPro data show global textile suppliers carry $15.65bn in annualised L/C exposure to Bangladesh, a payment system now running through a banking sector with 35.73 per cent NPLs. 
Every top 12 supplier country cut Q1 exposure YoY except the United States, up 53.7 per cent to $101 million. 
The divergence is the market’s first clear counterparty-risk signal, and it is already being paid.

title: Vietnam, Italy gain as global apparel imports fall 5%
summary:
Weak global apparel demand is accelerating a sourcing reset rather than an across-the-board decline.
Vietnam is gaining from reliable, large-scale sourcing, while Italy is benefiting from premium, near-market production.
India’s apparel exports continue to lag, suggesting policy support alone is insufficient without faster execution, stronger compliance and greater buyer confidence.

title: Sri Lanka’s garment exports dip 4.5% in Jan-May; May shows recovery
summary:
Sri Lanka’s apparel sector remains the backbone of industrial exports, contributing over 45 per cent despite weaker global demand.
While garment exports declined during January-May, May recorded a recovery, suggesting demand may be stabilising.
Falling textile imports also point to softer manufacturing activity and cautious sourcing across the supply chain.

title: Italian-Irish venture to set up footwear factory in Bangladesh
summary:
Italian and Irish-backed Deltaport Footwear will invest $21.6 million to set up a footwear factory at the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority Economic Zone in Mirsharai, Chattogram.
The unit will have an annual production capacity of around 3 million pairs.
The factory is expected to create 468 jobs and generate annual export earnings of about $37.5 million.

title: South Korean apparel imports up 1% to $4.8 bn in January-May 2026
summary:
South Korea's apparel imports rose 1 per cent year on year to $4.806 billion during January-May 2026, driven by higher knitted apparel imports and a stronger May performance.
However, exports of man-made filaments and knitted fabrics declined amid weak global textile demand and intensifying competition from lower-cost producers worldwide.

title: EU apparel imports reach $205.6 bn amid supplier squeeze
summary:
Europe has become the global battleground for apparel sourcing as more suppliers compete for slower import growth.
Rising volumes, falling unit prices, tighter compliance rules and stronger buyer leverage are squeezing margins.
Future competitiveness will depend less on low prices and more on speed, traceability, product mix and value-added manufacturing.

title: US’ Nike reports stable FY26 revenue amid market headwinds
summary:
Nike has reported flat FY26 revenue of $46.4 billion as North American growth offset weaker demand in China and EMEA. 
Wholesale sales increased, while Nike Direct and Converse declined. 
Despite lower annual profit, the company advanced its long-term growth strategy. 
In Q4, revenue dipped 1 per cent, but tariff recovery sharply lifted gross margin, net income, and earnings per share.

title: UK backs Philippines' path towards CPTPP accession
summary:
CPTPP parties will begin preparatory discussions with the Philippines, Indonesia, and the UAE after a virtual commission meeting recently. 
For apparel and textile exporters, any future Philippine accession could mean lower tariffs, simpler rules, and stronger supply-chain links. 
The talks do not guarantee accession or formal negotiations.

title: Türkiye's apparel exports fall 4.6% in Jan-May amid weak global demand
summary:
Türkiye's apparel exports fell 4.59 per cent year on year to $6.464 billion in January-May 2026 as weak demand continued to weigh on shipments.
The slowdown deepened in May, when exports dropped 13.85 per cent after April's brief recovery, amid cautious global buying, smaller orders, and rising competition from lower-cost sourcing destinations.

title: Turkiye’s $6.6 bn apparel exports chase new markets
summary:
Turkiye’s apparel exports show a strategic shift rather than a simple slowdown. 
Weak EU demand is being partly offset by growth in the Middle East, Eastern Europe, Africa and the Americas, but newer markets may not match Europe’s margins.  
Sustained growth will depend on leveraging textile integration, faster lead times, compliance and higher-value, design-led apparel.

title: South Korea's Misto Holdings unveils 2030 ESG sustainability roadmap
summary:
Misto Holdings has unveiled its 2030 Sustainability Roadmap, strengthening its data-driven ESG strategy with measurable climate, supply chain and governance targets. 
The company set 2030 GHG reduction goals, achieved 100 per cent Tier 1 supplier compliance participation, cancelled KRW 268.2 billion in shares to improve shareholder value, and retained strong global ESG ratings.
